items.title: Krylov dynamics of deformed oscillator chains: localization, ballistic spreading, and indeterminacy
items.summary: Krylov and spread complexity map quantum dynamics onto a quantum walk on a half-line whose hopping amplitudes are the Lanczos coefficients, so that Krylov dynamics is the theory of orthogonal polynomials and Jacobi operators. We use this correspondence to study Krylov chains generated by the two-parameter $(p,q)$-deformed oscillator, which interpolates between the Heisenberg--Weyl chain, the $q$-oscillator chain of double-scaled SYK, and chains with exponentially growing Lanczos coefficients.

items.title: Observation of programmable spatiotemporal quantum-inspired bits
items.summary: Coherent superposition allows information to be encoded in the geometry of physical states1-7. Preparing individual states, however, does not determine how they can be organized throughout a wave, because the wave propagation and modulation constrain the underlying interference.

items.title: Probing the Rung-Mott Insulator in Bosonic Two-Leg Ladders
items.summary: Mott insulators typically appear at integer densities, but certain lattice geometries or non-local interactions can stabilise Mott insulators at fractional densities. In this work, we study strongly interacting two-leg ladders using ultracold bosonic atoms around half-filling, and identify the rung-Mott insulating (RMI) phase through its characteristic rung occupation in site-resolved measurements.

items.title: Unbounded GHZ dimension from fixed-order multiphoton sources
items.summary: We study the local dimension of Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) states obtained by selecting events with one photon per output path. Each coherent source emits photons with a fixed internal label into a distinct set of paths, and the sets for each label partition the outputs.

items.title: Electrons in a hard-wall cylinder with helicoidal metric: time-reversal pairing, cubic anticrossings, and twist-activated dipole transitions
items.summary: We study the scalar Schrödinger equation in a helicoidal metric when the axial direction is closed by Dirichlet walls built into the operator domain. With hard walls, the axial derivative cannot be replaced by a traveling-wave factor, and in a rotationally symmetric spinless cavity, time reversal makes the levels with azimuthal numbers $m$ and $-m$ exactly degenerate.

items.title: Phase information and measurement in the Stochastic--Quantum correspondence
items.summary: The recently proposed stochastic-quantum correspondence establishes a connection between general stochastic processes and quantum dynamics, in which stochastic transition probabilities admit compatible representations on a Hilbert space, known as quantum lifts. We ask how the predictive information represented by off-diagonal degrees of freedom in the quantum lift is encoded within the stochastic description.

items.title: Optimal Trace Distance Estimation
items.summary: We present a trace distance estimator with optimal sample complexity. Specifically, the trace distance between two unknown $d$-dimensional quantum states can be estimated to within additive error $\varepsilon$ using \[ Θ\left(\frac{d^2}{\varepsilon^2\log^2(d)\max\left\{1,\varepsilon^2\log^2(d)\right\}}\right) \] samples of each quantum state.

items.title: Quantum Capacity with Incoherent Codes
items.summary: Arbitrarily weak depolarizing noise drives the quantum capacity to zero in every input basis when the encoder is restricted to incoherent operations. Even one qubit cannot then be sent reliably: if the output is replaced by the maximally mixed state with probability $\varepsilon\le1/2$, the entanglement fidelity is at most $1-\varepsilon/2$ at every block length.

items.title: Controlled teleportation of an unknown qutrit and its control power
items.summary: We propose a controlled quantum teleportation protocol for an arbitrary unknown qutrit using a nonmaximally entangled channel, with Charlie holding a qubit and Alice and Bob each holding a four-level particle. With the aid of an auxiliary qubit, the receiver can recover the input state probabilistically with unit fidelity.

items.title: The infinite-dimensional extended Bloch representation
items.summary: In the extended Bloch representation (EBR) of quantum mechanics, the Born probabilities of a measurement with N outcomes are the relative volumes of N regions of a simplex-shaped abstract membrane, whose points represent the "hidden" measurement interactions. However, when N tends to infinity, the volumes vanish and the uniform membrane concentrates at the center of the unit ball.

items.title: When Randomness Hides Quantum Simulation Errors
items.summary: Trotter formulas approximate quantum dynamics by discrete steps, but errors in measured observables can be much smaller than worst-case estimates. We investigate how this suppression depends on the degree of randomness in the input states.

items.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
items.summary: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$.

items.title: Perfect state transfer in Grover walks on generalized Bethe trees
items.summary: We completely classify the generalized Bethe trees $B(d_0,d_1,\ldots,d_{n-1})$ that exhibit perfect state transfer between vertex states in Grover walks. We prove that such a tree exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if it is a path or a uniform subdivision of either $B(2,3)$ or $B(1,2,3)$.

items.title: Machine Learning-Based Quantum Error Mitigation for Bound-State Simulations
items.summary: Noise in quantum devices remains a major challenge for reliable quantum simulations, making quantum error mitigation an important tool for improving their accuracy. Machine learning-based quantum error mitigation (ML-QEM) provides a useful approach, but its performance depends on the training datasets and may produce reconstructed quantum states that are not physically valid.

items.title: Electron spin relaxation and coherence times of silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
items.summary: Color defect centers carrying electron spins in solid crystals like diamond and silicon carbide (SiC) are promising candidates for qubits and quantum sensors, with SiC material being particularly interesting due to its compatibility with the existing semiconductor technology. Here we investigated the electron spin properties of silicon vacancy centers (V1 and V2) both electron spin $S = 3/2$ in 4H-SiC in the temperature range $T=80-300$~K using electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR).

items.title: Second-order asymptotics for the quantum and private capacities of the erasure channel
items.summary: An erasure channel either delivers a quantum system intact or tells the receiver that it was lost. How much quantum information, or secret classical information, can a finite block transmit without assistance?

items.title: Thermal state preparation with shallow quantum circuits
items.summary: Preparing thermal states on noisy quantum hardware requires circuits that remain shallow at low temperatures. Even when accurate classical state representations are available, compiling them into suitable circuits can be costly.

items.title: Quantum Coherence and Basis-Dependent Correlations in Quantum Systems
items.summary: Quantum coherence and quantum correlations are two fundamental features of quantum systems and are closely related in various quantum information tasks. In general, due to the existence of correlations, the amount of coherence in a bipartite state should be no less than that in the reduced states.

items.title: A quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder for robust anomaly detection at the LHC
items.summary: Model-agnostic searches for new physics at the Large Hadron Collider utilise unsupervised anomaly detection, where quantum and neuromorphic detectors represent potential approaches. We develop the first fully spiking variational autoencoder, a quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder (QSVAE), built on the quantum-inspired leaky integrate-and-fire (QLIF) neuron.

items.title: Rydberg Constraint Ensembles for Nonnative Binary Optimization
items.summary: Rydberg blockade can exclude the configuration that minimizes a binary objective. We expand its finite penalties into a weighted ensemble of exclusion graphs. The full ensemble preserves the ground energy, and the interactions remaining on each graph set its local detunings.

items.title: Improving Quantum Oblivious Transfer using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
items.summary: While quantum protocols for oblivious transfer can be built from weaker assumptions than classical ones, the current protocols remain highly impractical due to stringent security bounds that demand a large amount of quantum communication. In this work, we propose an enhancement to quantum oblivious transfer protocols by leveraging zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs).

items.title: The role of composition rules in an axiomatic derivation of quantum mechanics
items.summary: Local discriminability and purification are two key axioms in an information-theoretic axiomatization of quantum mechanics as proposed by G. M. D'Ariano et al.

items.title: Entanglement between distant spins in a polarized magnet forms a $d$-wave clover
items.summary: Spin-orbit coupling makes a polarized magnet a source of virtual spin-flip pairs. These pairs entangle distant spins: the symmetry of the coupling fixes the angular pattern, and the flips they leave behind end it at a distance of order the inverse spin-orbit angle.

items.title: Transfer tensor description of driven inhomogeneous quantum systems
items.summary: The transfer tensor method (TTM) extrapolates open quantum system dynamics from short-time trajectories by encoding memory effects in a discrete hierarchy of transfer tensors. Standard TTM relies on time-translational invariance (TTI) of the dynamical maps, which is broken by time-dependent driving or coherent control.

items.title: Low-Degree Torus Approximations of the AND Function and $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ Circuits
items.summary: Torus polynomials, real polynomials evaluated modulo one, were proposed by Bhrushundi, Hosseini, Lovett, and Rao as a route to $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ lower bounds. We prove degree upper bounds for torus polynomials approximating a function on every input.

items.title: Toward light-controlled transverse Wigner ordering in attosecond electron beams
items.summary: Kinetic fluctuations and space-charge expansion hinder Wigner ordering in free-electron beams. Here we propose a laser-driven route toward transient, substrate-free Wigner ordering that combines photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) attosecond bunching, synchronized magnetic focusing, and spatial preconditioning.

items.title: Validity and maximum violation of the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound for linear stabilizer codes
items.summary: Entanglement-assisted quantum codes protect quantum information with entangled pairs shared in advance, and the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound of Brun, Devetak and Hsieh is the standard estimate of how many pairs they consume. Codes that violate it at large distance are known.

items.title: Universal state merging for almost i.i.d. states
items.summary: In quantum state merging, Alice aims to transfer her share of a bipartite state to Bob while preserving the joint state with a purifying reference. For i.i.d. copies of $ρ_{AB}$, the optimal asymptotic net entanglement cost is $S(A|B)_ρ$ ebits per pair.

items.title: Eliminating Incompatibility in Quantum Multiparameter Estimation with Antiparallel Probes
items.summary: The simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters is fundamentally constrained by complementarity and measurement incompatibility, which limits the sensitivity of quantum measurement devices by preventing the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) from being saturated. We show that antiparallel probe configurations can overcome this limitation when the dynamics of the parameter encoding preserve the said configurations.

items.title: Beyond Classical Minimax Rates: Quantum Sampling in Gradient-Based Simulation Optimization
items.summary: We study gradient-based search for a class of convex simulation optimization problems with gradients estimated from noisy outputs. With independent outputs, the optimal classical convergence rate for the expected objective gap is of order $O(N^{-2/3})$, where $N$ is the query budget.

items.title: QuOptLab: Advancing Quantum Optics Experiments with an AI Agent
items.summary: Recent advances in AI-assisted theoretical research suggest that AI agents can contribute to research-level problems. Whether they can also advance experimental research by conducting experiments, analyzing the results, and proposing better experimental designs remains an open question.

items.title: Schur saturation and the Clifford ceiling in qudit CSS codes
items.summary: Orthogonality-type conditions (triorthogonality in the qubit setting and its prime-dimensional analogues), are the primary algebraic screening criterion for transversal non-Clifford gate constructions in CSS codes. In every known positive construction the certificate is accompanied by a non-Clifford logical gate, leaving open whether a CSS family can satisfy these conditions to arbitrarily high order while admitting no such gate.

items.title: Hybrid correlation generation with finite shared randomness
items.summary: Finite shared randomness can reduce the use of a prescribed two-qubit source in a hybrid model. Each party has two fixed binary projective measurements, and the protocol reproduces the resulting joint outcome distributions exactly.

items.title: Coherent meson-baryon conversion in a cold-atom non-Abelian lattice gauge simulator
items.summary: Quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the non-Abelian gauge theory of quarks and gluons, provides a microscopic description of strongly interacting matter, including hadron structure and dynamics. Real-time dynamics and finite-density properties of these systems remain challenging for conventional Monte Carlo methods because of sign problems.

items.title: A machine learning architecture for scaling of holographic quantum circuits
items.summary: We describe an architecture and workflow for learning and generalizing the syntax and parameters of holographic quantum circuits (HQCs), which are natural quantum circuit analogs of classical tensor networks. An HQC uses mid-circuit measurements and resets on a small subset of "physical" qubits whose measurement outcomes become correlated through coupling with a register of persistent "ancilla" qubits, analogous to the physical and bond indices of a tensor network.

items.title: Geometric Control of Electronic Decoherence in a Chiral Spin-Orbit Coupled Helix
items.summary: While chirality is known to impact chemical and optical properties of molecular systems, as well as their biological function, far less is known about its impact on quantum coherence. By considering a chiral helix as a paradigmatic model, we show that within the Born-Markov regime, changing the degree of helical twist can be used to modulate the electronic decoherence rate.

items.title: A colored look at anyons and parastatistics
items.summary: Color Lie (super)algebras were introduced in 1978 by Rittenberg and Wyler as generalizations of ordinary Lie (super)algebras. These color structures, graded by abelian groups, are defined by brackets which satisfy generalized Jacobi identities.

items.title: From outcome exclusion to measurement simulation
items.summary: While quantum state exclusion has received considerable attention, the analogous task of measurement outcome exclusion remains less explored. Here we develop a quantitative description of outcome exclusion and extend the resulting framework to obtain necessary and sufficient criteria for measurement simulation by quantum pre-processing and classical post-processing.

items.title: Temporal Soliton Waves in Modern Fiber Laser Systems
items.summary: This chapter provides a comprehensive survey of temporal soliton-wave in modern fiber systems. Temporal soliton waves constitute a broad class of nonlinear localized structures in modern fiber laser systems, arising from different balances among dispersion, nonlinearity, gain, loss, spectral filtering, and various forms of cavity coupling.

items.title: Exact approach to double- and triple-excitation bound state in open quantum systems
items.summary: The determination of multiple-excitation bound state in open quantum systems is of broad interest in quantum physics. While the emergence of double- or triple-excitation bound state has been demonstrated in certain specific situations, their universality and exact solvability remain elusive.

items.title: Symmetry-constrained order hierarchy of connected optical responses in a five-level Rydberg-EIT medium
items.summary: Determining the connected many-body correlations required for a nonlinear optical response of a given order is a central challenge in interacting open quantum systems. We establish a symmetrybased selection rule for connected optical responses in a driven-dissipative Rydberg-EIT model.

items.title: Probing the inner structure of bound states
items.summary: We show how constructing a composite particle eigenstate reveals its internal structure. Using quantum subspace expansion (QSE), we optimize states with different sets of operators and use their fidelities with the full QSE state to measure the importance of each added operator type.

items.title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
items.summary: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) encode the non-perturbative structure of hadrons in terms of their partonic constituents. They are defined through matrix elements containing parton operators that are connected by a Wilson line along a light-front direction, which makes them difficult to access in Euclidean lattice calculations.

items.title: Light-cone distributions of vector and scalar bound states in the Schwinger model from tensor networks
items.summary: Light-cone distributions encode the partonic structure of hadrons, but they involve real-time correlations that Euclidean lattice methods cannot access directly. We compute the parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of the vector and scalar meson bound states of the massive Schwinger model with tensor networks.

items.title: Phase matching of high-order harmonics driven by a combined coherent and bright squeezed vacuum field
items.summary: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) driven by non-classical light provides new insights into light-matter interactions and paves the way to quantum attosecond spectroscopy. Achieving phase matching is vital for generating bright HHG sources, while it has received comparatively limited attention in quantum-light-driven HHG.

items.title: Universal quantum gate set for multimode Schrödinger cat states stabilized by nonlocal dissipation engineering
items.summary: Schr\"odinger cat states provide a hardware-efficient platform for bosonic quantum error correction by encoding logical information in protected manifolds of harmonic oscillators. While previous work has demonstrated the dissipative stabilization of multimode Schr\"odinger cat states as robust quantum memories, a framework for universal quantum computation has remained unavailable.

items.title: Quantum Annealing Complexity and Stochastic Quantum Control
items.summary: This thesis investigates two central challenges for quantum computing: identifying when quantum annealing can offer a computational advantage, and developing effective methods to control realistic quantum systems. It establishes complexity bounds for an adiabatic algorithm for combinatorial optimization, showing a universal quadratic advantage while highlighting the practical difficulty of realizing the required schedule.

items.title: Fixed-preparation short-time reconstruction of class-D BdG endpoint masses
items.summary: In one-dimensional class-D superconductors, the relative signs of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) masses at particle-hole-invariant momenta fix the bulkinvariant. Band energies and transition-frequency peak locations alone cannot determine these signs.

items.title: The waggle dance in honeybees: a language - beyond metaphor
items.summary: The waggle dance reports an outbound flight vector with a ritualized whole-body movement to a location in the environment surrounding the bee colony. This informative gesture is embedded in the cognitive faculties involved in organizing the social life inside and outside the hive during foraging for food and finding a new nest site.

items.title: Actualization and the Quantum Mechanical Universe: Dissolving the Gap
items.summary: The actualization gap—the apparent discontinuity between the classical probability distribution delivered by decoherence and the single definite outcome that appears in experience—has been treated in the foundations literature as an outstanding problem in the physics of quantum measurement. This paper argues that the gap is not a physical problem and admits no physical solution.

items.title: Does Total Knowledge Mute Emotion? A Thought Experiment using Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper examines whether comprehensive knowledge acquisition attenuates emotional experience through a thought experiment that uses large language models (LLMs). We propose that LLMs, which possess extensive propositional knowledge yet lack phenomenal consciousness, serve as philosophical instruments for isolating the knowledge variable from other cognitive attributes.

items.title: Virtual reality as a neural state-modulating technology: EEG complexity during VR gameplay versus VR gameplay viewing
items.summary: Pharmacological agents and brain stimulation can modulate conscious states, but offer limited control over the structure of the experience itself. Virtual reality (VR) can alter subjective experience while allowing its structure to be experimentally controlled.

items.title: Effects of auditory sensory stimulation on consciousness and physiological parameters among individuals with disorders of consciousness: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: Objective: To systematically evaluate the effects of auditory sensory stimulation (SS) on consciousness levels and physiological parameters in patients with disorders of consciousness (DOC). Furthermore, this study aimed to explore intervention characteristics based on the frequency, intensity, time, and type (FITT) framework that may influence treatment effects and to investigate potential sources of between-study heterogeneity.

items.title: Nāgārjunian Madhyamaka and relational quantum mechanics: the limits of relational foundationalism
items.summary: Comparisons between Mahāyāna Buddhism and quantum physics often equate emptiness with indeterminacy, dependent arising with quantum relationality and entanglement with universal interconnection. Such equations conflate four levels: experimental results, mathematical formalism, interpretations of quantum theory and metaphysical extrapolations.

items.title: Scaling Limits of Time-averaged Distributions for Symmetric Quantum Walks on Hypercubes
items.summary: We study continuous-time and discrete-time quantum walks on the hypercube $\{0,1\}^d$ associated with symmetric random walks, that is, random walks whose transition probabilities depend only on the Hamming distance, using the Hamming scheme and Krawtchouk polynomials. For continuous-time walks, we show that the time-averaged distribution of the Hamming distance is a discrete arcsine law whenever the eigenvalues are distinct.

items.title: Adaptive ghost Gutzwiller dynamics of Hubbard model quenches across coupling strengths over extended times
items.summary: Following the real-time dynamics of correlated electrons to extended times, at all interaction strengths, remains an open challenge. We address it with an adaptive time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation (td-gGA).

items.title: Genuinely Quantum Algorithms for Bio-inspired Meta-heuristic Optimization
items.summary: Quantum computation offers a promising pathway toward advancing meta-heuristic optimization, particularly in Nature-inspired paradigms such as genetic algorithms and swarm intelligence. This study conducts a systematic literature review of fifteen major meta-heuristics to assess current efforts toward their quantum realization.

items.title: Graduate training in quantum information science and engineering: Lessons, challenges, and a roadmap from the NSF research traineeship programs

Setting down what our programs have learned so that others can use it, contest it, and test it, we work through the central tensions that every QISE graduate program must negotiate: between depth in a home discipline and breadth across the field, between structured…

items.title: Opposite post-processing orders of fermionic horizon channels and their quantum-resource monotonicity
items.summary: Studies of relativistic quantum information in noninertial and black-hole settings often focus on specific input states and resource functionals, leaving the common origin of recurring monotonic trends in quantum resources and correlations unclear. In this work, we identify a common channel-ordering structure from the complementary exterior and interior reductions of the effective single-mode fermionic horizon transformation, representing the physically accessible and inaccessible sectors, respectively.

items.title: Quantum Sensing as an Optimization-Inference Stack
items.summary: Every data science pipeline begins with a measurement. When that measurement is made by a quantum mechanical system—exploiting superposition, entanglement, and coherence—the sensor can in principle surpass the classical shot-noise precision limit.

items.title: Parameter-shift rules for gradients in boson sampling experiments
items.summary: Using a robust photon loss model for photonic quantum experiments, we derive n th order parameter-shift rules (PSRs) for computing gradients of Fock boson sampling transition probabilities where n photons are sent into a lossy interferometer. We also show that one cannot naturally generalize this gradient recipe to the case of Gaussian boson sampling.

items.title: Quantum Graph Neural Networks: Architectures, Trainability, and Applications
items.summary: Quantum graph neural networks (QGNNs) apply parametrized quantum circuits to graph-structured data, with the aim of overcoming limits of classical graph neural networks in scalability, expressivity, and long-range information flow. Since the first Hamiltonian-based model in 2019, the field has produced many architectures, applications, and claims, but the evidence behind them has not been assessed systematically.

items.title: Almost-quantum correlations violate information causality
items.summary: Information causality (IC), a generalization of the no-signalling principle, states that communicating m classical bits cannot give the receiver access to more than m bits of information about the sender's independent data. Although IC holds in quantum theory and excludes a broad class of supra-quantum correlations, its validity for the almost-quantum set has remained open.

items.title: Measurement-informed dynamical decoupling for fidelity preservation on large-scale quantum processors
items.summary: Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a key technique for suppressing decoherence and preserving the performance of quantum algorithms. We introduce a measurement-based DD (MDD) protocol that determines control unitary gates from partial measurements of noisy subsystems, with measurement overhead scaling linearly with the number of subsystems.

Predictive coding neuroscience is a clear example: its literature spans computational theory, electrophysiology, imaging, behavior, and modeling, creating a synthesis problem that conventional meta-analysis cannot easily resolve.

items.summary: Quantum theory remains empirically unmatched in its domain, yet its conceptual foundations—measurement, the status of the wavefunction, and the classical limit—remain contested. A research programme due to Barandes reframes unitary quantum mechanics in terms of indivisible (non-Markovian) stochastic processes on configuration space, with unistochastic transition matrices supplying the bridge to complex amplitudes.

items.title: Exploring Discrete Algorithms in Quantum Computing
items.summary: Quantum computing introduces a new computational paradigm by extending the classical binary representation of information through quantum bits, which can exist in superposed states and exhibit entanglement. This work presents a systematic study of fundamental concepts, computational mechanisms, and discrete algorithms in quantum computing.

items.title: Quantum Random Number Generators: principles, practical challenges and mainstream implementations
items.summary: Quantum random number generators have become a cornerstone technology for modern digital cryptography, including key generation, quantum key distribution, and post-quantum cryptographic systems. While existing reviews typically concentrate on specific entropy sources or implementation platforms, a comprehensive perspective encompassing the complete QRNG pipeline remains largely absent.

items.title: Liquid Integrated Network as Candidate Substrate for Artificial Consciousness
items.summary: Whether artificial intelligence (AI) system allows for generating machine consciousness has been a “grand challenge” which however must be answered in this day and age. Most contemporary AI is implemented on large scale solid-state electronic hardware, whereas biological consciousness is supported by much smaller sized space within a fluid-rich brain.

items.title: Endogenous suspension of phenomenal consciousness during extended cessation: Regional homogeneity analysis of multi-participant 7T fMRI of an advanced meditative endpoint
items.summary: Extended cessation (EC) is a rare advanced meditative state characterized by the voluntary absence of reportable phenomenal experience, followed by reproducible aftereffects including immense mental clarity, equanimity, and peace. EC offers an endogenous model for investigating the mechanisms of consciousness.

items.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
items.summary: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions.

items.title: When lies look like noise: certifying untrusted entanglement swapping
items.summary: Entanglement swapping lets quantum repeaters distribute entanglement over long distances, a prerequisite for the quantum internet. We study its security in a noisy network whose intermediate nodes perform the quantum operations faithfully but may misreport the classical outcome that end users rely on.

items.title: SynDebug: A Framework to Debug Logic Bugs in Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Programs
items.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) introduces substantial systems-level complexity through quantum error correction (QEC), making debugging FTQC programs challenging. Existing quantum debugging approaches primarily target logical-level circuits and do not naturally support debugging within realistic FTQC execution flows.

items.title: The entangled loop: Emotion, interference and hierarchy in the architecture of consciousness
items.summary: Why does consciousness feel like something, and why is experience unified rather than fragmented? We propose that these properties arise from an entangled trefoil of emotion, interference-based inference and hierarchical orchestration, shaped by the thermodynamic constraint that living systems must remain far from equilibrium using limited energy.

items.title: What Counts as Intelligence?
items.summary: This essay examines what justifies attributing intelligence to artificial systems without conflating functional competence, biological cognition, conscious experience, and responsible discernment. It develops syntropy as a philosophical criterion of relational coherence, continual reorientation, and responsibility, rather than as a new scientific law or a closed ontology.

items.title: A relativistic gravitisation of quantum theory?
items.summary: We develop a model, that we call local semiclassical gravity, based on the distributional semiclassical Einstein field equations (EFEs) sourced by the local quantum state, i.e. the reduced density matrix of the local system updated by collapses (only) in its past light cone.

items.title: Quantum Symmetry and Entanglement Horizons: Theory, Photonic Systems, and Quantum Inspired Data Analytics
items.summary: This book examines the role of translational symmetry in shaping and stabilising quantum entanglement across spatial and temporal domains. Building on foundational concepts from the EPR paradox and Bell’s theorem, it introduces a nodal–antinodal framework to explain coherence preservation and entanglement amplification.

items.title: Indefinite causal order with definite Bohmian trajectories for the quantum switch
items.summary: We analyze the notion of indefinite causal order (ICO) from the standpoint of the deterministic de Broglie--Bohm theory, based on the notion of trajectories in configuration space. More precisely, we study the physics of the quantum switch (QS) interferometer within a Bohmian framework and show how the notion of causality is preserved in this approach.

items.title: Qualiaphobic artificial neural networks (and why to build them)
items.summary: This paper introduces qualiaphobic AI: artificial neural network architectures that are hostile to theories of consciousness. I show that qualiaphobia can be well-justified by knowledge about theories of consciousness, like when such theories are trivial or unfalsifiable or contradicted by overwhelming scientific evidence.
